references.why: Allusion recast by the writer (applied to evil things unheard of in Christian lands); Segond's agreement with « des choses » (vues/entendues) does not fit the sentence.

Allusion inside David Brainerd's epigraph (KJV 'taken captive by him at his will'), recast by Brainerd with 'Satan'; Segond's wording ('qui s’est emparé d’eux pour les soumettre à sa volonté') does not fit the quoted sentence.
Author paraphrases in the present tense about the Indian potter (Segond: « Il en refit un autre vase, Tel qu’il trouva bon de le faire »).
Allusion to KJV 'before the gods will I sing praise unto thee'; Segond reads « en la présence de Dieu », but the author's point is the idol gods in possession of the land; re-personed.
Re-personed allusion (thy → his, us → one soul); Segond's « du milieu des nations » rendered « du milieu des païens » to keep the author's 'heathen'; rest follows Segond's wording.
Allusion ('the Ruler of Darkness') singularised; Segond has « les princes de ce monde de ténèbres ».
KJV wording 'intrude into those things which he hath not seen'; Segond reads « s’abandonne à ses visions », which does not carry the author's words.
Allusion re-personed into a prayer and extended ('with each of them'); keeps Segond's 'travail de son âme' but Segond's syntax ('il rassasiera ses regards') does not fit the sentence.
Re-personed from 'en vous' to 'en eux' (the converts); otherwise Segond's wording.

The author quotes a Revised-Version-margin wording ('captives of the Terrible'); 'the Terrible' is the chapter's title and personified adversary throughout, which Segond renders 'tyran' (and 'juste' in v24), so the wording is kept in her sense.
Segond wording except the author's plural « brothers' » (the millions), kept: « tes frères » for Segond's « ton frère ».
KJV 'there is sorrow on the sea; it cannot be quiet'; Segond reads « C’est une mer en tourmente », which loses the 'sorrow' the author applies to the dirge. Second half follows Segond.
A line of the widow's Tamil dirge, re-personed echo of 'I sought him, but I found him not'; not a quotation of Scripture as such.
Explicitly quoted from Conybeare and Howson's translation (first person, 'this very end'), not the KJV; rendered from that version.
Allusive noun phrase ('Mortality swallowed up in Life'); Segond has « afin que ce qui est mortel soit englouti par la vie ».
Conybeare and Howson's 'for this very End', the chapter's key word; Segond has « pour cela ».

Allusive prayer echoing Ezekiel 37:9 ('Come... O breath, and breathe'); Segond has « Esprit, viens des quatre vents, souffle », but the chapter's argument runs on 'Breath' (Souffle), so kept her wording.
KJV 'almost persuaded'; Segond (« Tu vas bientôt me persuader ») lacks 'almost', on which her next sentence depends ('only almost, not quite').
She gives her own rendering built on the Tamil word for verdigris ('so as to remove thy verdigris'); only the opening clause matches Segond, the rest is her point and cannot be Segond's « scories ».
Short devotional phrase 'Christ in me' (cf. Galatians 2:20, Colossians 1:27), not a verbatim verse; Segond has « Christ qui vit en moi ».
KJV 'We have not wrought any deliverance in the earth'; Segond reads « Le pays n’est pas sauvé », and her next line ('We have not') depends on the first-person 'we have not wrought'.
KJV idiom 'we believe to see' (Ps 27:13, 'I had believed to see'), re-personed and built on 'believe'; Segond has « sûr de voir ».
Blended allusion: Job 12:16 ('With him is strength') + Ephesians 3:7 ('effectual working'); not a verbatim quotation.
Re-personed ('abide in Him without Whom we can do nothing'); Segond: « sans moi vous ne pouvez rien faire ».
Allusion adapted to the context: Segond's « Et qui est suffisant pour ces choses? » applied to delivering a soul.
Address to God re-personed from Segond « Qui seul fait des prodiges » (third person) into the second person, as in the quoted prayer.
Allusion inside a quoted letter; the writer says 'out of darkness into His light' without Segond's 'admirable', and the verb/subject are re-cast around 'the heathen'.
Re-personed allusion ('has a name to live, but is dead') applied to 'many a pastor, catechist, teacher'; follows Segond's 'tu passes pour être vivant, et tu es mort' in the third person.

Her prayer to 'the mighty God of revivals' turns on 'revive' (KJV); Segond has 'Accomplis ton œuvre'. Kept 'revive' (fais revivre), Segond's wording elsewhere ('dans le cours des années', 'manifeste-la'); the verse is also rearranged/repeated as she quotes it.
Re-personed allusion (applied to 'the brave of old'): Segond's 'qui affronta la mort, ... Sur les hauteurs des champs' recast in the plural.
Author quotes KJV 'against the mighty'; Segond reads 'parmi les hommes vaillants', which would reverse her sense (fighting against the mighty). Segond's 'au secours de l’Éternel' kept.
Blended quotation: Mark 8:35 ('for my sake and the gospel's', Segond wording kept) with 'shall find it' (Matthew 10:39 'la retrouvera'); Segond Mark 8:35 has 'la sauvera'.
Adapted allusion: 'thy brother's blood' re-personed to 'our brothers', our sisters' blood' and 'unto me' to 'unto God'; built on Segond's 'La voix du sang de ton frère crie de la terre jusqu’à moi'.

Echo of KJV 'there remaineth yet very much land to be possessed'; the author's following 'arise and possess it' depends on 'possess', which Segond ('le pays qui te reste à soumettre est très grand') lacks.
Loose paraphrase reported in the mouth of a Hindu objector (cf. Mark 11:23), not a quotation; no reference in source.
Livingstone quotes the clause standalone with 'a sparrow' as subject; Segond's 'il n’en tombe pas un à terre sans la volonté de votre Père' is kept but the subject supplied. Uncited in source.
Allusion re-personed into third person (Segond: 'Ne remplis-je pas, moi, les cieux et la terre?').
Allusion re-personed as a relative clause (Segond: 'Tout a été créé par lui').

Paraphrase in present tense within the author's sentence; Segond wording kept otherwise ('Comme un berger, il paîtra son troupeau, Il prendra les agneaux dans ses bras, Et les portera dans son sein').

A child's retelling of a martyr story echoing Jesus' words to Judas, re-personed to the plural addressed to the executioners and reworded ('what you are going to do'); Segond's 'fais-le promptement' kept as the echo.
Allusion, singularised and applied to Hinduism (Segond: « sépulcres blanchis … au-dedans, sont pleins d’ossements de morts »); key words kept from Segond but not a verbatim substring.
Allusion re-personed to readers' hearts (Segond: « Répands ton cœur comme de l’eau »).
Allusion re-shaped (Segond: « Lève tes mains vers lui pour la vie de tes enfants »).
Re-personed and pluralised (« daughters of our people »); Segond words kept where possible.
Allusion generalised by the author to 'one's bones'; Segond's 'feu dévorant qui est renfermé dans mes os' re-personed and shortened.
Allusion in the plural ('voices crying in the wilderness', KJV wording); Segond's Isaiah 40:3 reads 'Une voix crie: Préparez au désert'.
Recast from imperatives into a subordinate clause; 'heavy burdens' is the KJV reading where Segond has 'liens de la servitude'.
KJV Isaiah 9:5 ('every battle of the warrior is with confused noise') differs in sense from Segond 9:4 (footwear and garments given to the flames); author's wording kept.
Author quotes the KJV 'slaves and souls of men'; Segond has 'de corps et d’âmes d’hommes', which would lose her point.
KJV Ps 34:8 = Segond 34:9. Segond has « Sentez », but the author's point hangs on TASTING (the queen who proved the truth by tasting the food), so « goûtez » is kept; the rest is Segond's wording.
Allusion to « Laissez venir à moi les petits enfants » (KJV "suffer ... forbid them not"), recast in the third person about this child; Segond's verb « laisser venir » kept.

Verse paraphrase inside a quoted poem ("whatsoe'er is done / Unto Thy weakest and Thy humblest one, / Is even done to Thee"), re-personed as an address to God and fitted to the verse line; echoes Segond's « c’est à moi que vous les avez faites ».
Author's variant 'teach us how to pray'; kept her 'how'.
Re-personed allusion ('He goeth before') applied to God, from Segond's « il marche devant elles ».
Allusive address 'Searcher of hearts' turned into a prayer to God; Segond « celui qui sonde les cœurs » re-personed.
Poetic quotation alluding to Cain's 'Am I my brother's keeper?', not a verse quotation; uses Segond's « gardien de mon frère » vocabulary.
Allusion re-personed to the mourning family (third person, 'ceux qui' for Segond's 'les autres qui'); keeps Segond's 'vous affligiez' verb and 'n’ont point d’espérance'.

Allusion paraphrasing Abraham's faith after the RV reading (he 'considered' the facts); Segond (TR) says 'il ne considéra point', so the author's sense is kept; 'ne douta point' and 'fut fortifié' follow Segond 4:20.
Allusion re-personed to the third person plural, with the author's contrast added.
Popular paraphrase quoted from others ('nations are born in a day'), not the verse's wording.
Author's abridged exclamation 'Worthy is the Lamb to receive!'; Segond's full sentence ('L’agneau qui a été immolé est digne de recevoir…') cannot be cut to this fragment verbatim
KJV conditional 'If thou forbear to deliver…'; Segond is imperative ('Délivre ceux…'); Segond's phrases 'ceux qu’on traîne à la mort' and 'ceux qu’on va égorger' kept inside the conditional frame
Loose allusion ('Loose it, and let it go') addressed by the Lord to one person about a thing held back; Segond's plural 'Déliez-le, et laissez-le aller' put in the singular
Author's point is a Voice heard in stillness (KJV 'there was a voice'); Segond reads 'il se faisait un bruit'
The author's appeal rests on KJV 'Is it nothing to you'; Segond opens 'Je m’adresse à vous'. Segond's 'vous tous qui passez ici' and 'Regardez et voyez' kept
Quoted as a bare fragment ('Herein is love'); Segond's 'Et cet amour consiste…' does not stand alone
Author quotes the 'reflecting, as in a mirror' reading; Segond has 'contemplons'
Re-personed to 'we' as a question; Segond's verb 'saisir' kept
